name: Duration Neglect
description: When people remember an experience later, its total length often matters less than a few standout moments. Memory of the episode is weighted weakly by duration and more strongly by how it felt at its peak and ending.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to onboarding journeys, support recoveries, checkout flows, and service design where remembered experience matters. It should not be overextended into the claim that objective duration never matters — task time still affects abandonment and usability in ways remembered evaluation does not capture.
prevalence_note: Known in Kahneman-adjacent service-design and customer-experience discussions, but far less often named explicitly than Peak-End Rule in mainstream UX practice.

findings.description: Retrospective evaluations of affective episodes were only weakly influenced by how long the episodes lasted; remembered evaluation tracked standout moments much more than total duration, the core duration-neglect pattern.
findings.source_title: Duration neglect in retrospective evaluations of affective episodes.
findings.source_venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
